bench: Agentic baseline (E1): an external LLM agent drives the validated tools, audited for no-fabrication
question: When a real LLM agent (not the deterministic state machine) drives PEN-STACK's validated tools, does every number in its trace equal a direct tool call (no fabrication)? Does this hold across the model-capability range?
method: For each write-planning goal, the LLM (via pen_stack.agent.orchestrator.run_agent) plans and calls the validated design tools itself; pen_stack.validate.agent_eval.no_fabrication audits that every quantity in the returned plan is traceable to a tool result.  = the LLM actually drove the loop (not the deterministic fallback). Goals answered in prose (tool_calls=0) still pass because they emit no ungrounded quantity.
goals: insert a durable cassette at AAVS1
write into CCR5 for HIV resistance
place a durable transgene at CLYBL

deterministic_gate.note: the grounded state machine (no LLM); runs everywhere incl. CI

finding: Across three models spanning tiny-local (Qwen2.5-1.5B) to frontier (NVIDIA Nemotron-120B, Anthropic Claude), the LLM agent drove the validated tools on every goal (12/12 llm-driven) and the no-fabrication audit passed for all: every number in every trace equalled a direct tool call. The architecture, not the model, guarantees grounding - even a 1.5B model fabricates nothing when it must route quantities through the tools.

provenance.reproduce: python bench/run.py --agent  (with a reachable provider set in configs/llm.yaml)
provenance.note: nemotron+claude run against their cloud APIs (keys gitignored); qwen2.5:1.5b runs locally via Ollama.
